before: and the history of the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams (as); all of it is knowledge about God.
after: and the history of the Prophet ﷺ and the Imams (as). All of it is knowledge about God.
why: summing-up after a list, not a mirror; own sentence

before: Sheikh Bahmanpour gives a definition of mysticism: the urge to reach out to the infinite through knowledge by presence.
after: Sheikh Bahmanpour defines mysticism as the urge to reach out to the infinite through knowledge by presence.
why: two colons in the paragraph; folded

before: Every description says that it is brown or square or useful, and none says what
after: Every description says that it is brown, square, or useful, and none says what

before: Apart from the proof that He exists, the rest is negative knowledge: each statement says what God is not, and none says what He is.
after: Apart from the proof that He exists, the rest is negative knowledge, in which each statement says what God is not and none says what He is.
why: second colon in the paragraph; which-clause

before: We cannot know God's essence; what ʿirfan seeks is His attributes, known positively:
after: We cannot know God's essence. What ʿirfan seeks is His attributes, known positively:
why: second half much heavier than the first; own sentence

before: A sense of God already lives there, however faint: a vague idea of God that we carry inside us.
after: We carry a sense of God inside us, however faint.
why: 'a vague idea of God' renames 'a sense of God'; second colon in the paragraph

before: He claimed for it a rationalised mysticism: he gave rational argument to what the mystics know only by experience.
after: He claimed for it a rationalised mysticism, giving rational argument to what the mystics know only by experience.
why: second colon in the paragraph; participle

before: he writes, "is the greatest of veils"; yet "one has to approach a veil in order to tear it into shreds".
after: he writes, "is the greatest of veils", yet "one has to approach a veil in order to tear it into shreds".
why: 'yet' turn is a next step, not a mirror
